content.user_title: Triage GitHub Issues With Clear Replies
content.value_statement: Maintainers often need to understand issue reports before they answer. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through diagnosis, classification, decision support, and reply drafting.
actual_capabilities: Collects issue context from a user-provided GitHub issue or repository.
Guides code investigation from entry points to downstream handlers.
Classifies reports as bugs, architecture limits, feature requests, or usage questions.
Compares fix scope, testability, user impact, and workaround options.
Drafts professional GitHub replies for maintainer review before posting.
limitations: It does not guarantee access to private repositories or issue content.
It depends on the assistant having suitable repository context.
It does not replace maintainer judgment on roadmap or priority decisions.
It should not publish comments without explicit user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Handle bug reports
use_cases.description: Trace reported behavior through the codebase, identify likely causes, and prepare a clear maintainer response.

use_cases.title: Review feature requests
use_cases.description: Separate new capability requests from defects, estimate implementation cost, and explain product tradeoffs.

use_cases.title: Support repository users
use_cases.description: Turn incomplete user reports into structured questions, workaround guidance, and polite follow-up replies.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize an issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a single issue report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to read the GitHub issue I provide. Summarize the user environment, reproduction steps, expected behavior, actual behavior, and missing information.

prompt_templates.title: Find the root cause
prompt_templates.scenario: Code investigation after issue context is clear.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to inspect the relevant code path for this issue. Show the files, line references, call flow, and the likely root cause.

prompt_templates.title: Classify and decide
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to classify this issue as a bug, architecture limit, feature request, or usage question. Recommend whether to fix it, defer it, or suggest a workaround.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a maintainer response
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a researched issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a GitHub reply based on the diagnosis and decision. Explain the current design, user impact, workaround, and next steps.

output_examples.input: A user reports that a setting is ignored after restart.
output_examples.output: The report is treated as a likely bug. The response explains the affected setting, the suspected persistence path, the files to inspect, and a request for version details.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a workflow the product was not designed to support.
output_examples.output: The issue is classified as an architecture limit or feature request. The reply explains the design boundary, available workaround, estimated implementation cost, and possible future direction.

output_examples.input: A maintainer needs to answer a frustrated user professionally.
output_examples.output: The draft thanks the user, avoids blame, summarizes the finding, gives concrete next steps, and asks for confirmation before posting.

best_practices: Read the full issue before drawing conclusions.
Trace the complete code path before naming a root cause.
Get user confirmation before publishing any GitHub reply.
anti_patterns: Do not classify an issue from the title alone.
Do not blame users for unsupported workflows.
Do not promise fixes without checking scope and test conditions.

faq.question: Does this skill post GitHub comments automatically?
faq.answer: No. It requires user confirmation before any reply is posted.

faq.question: Can it analyze private repository issues?
faq.answer: Only when the assistant has authorized access to the repository and issue content.

faq.question: What issue types does it support?
faq.answer: It supports bug reports, feature requests, architecture limits, and usage questions.

faq.question: Does it write code fixes?
faq.answer: It focuses on triage and response drafting. Code changes require a separate implementation step.

faq.question: Can non-technical maintainers use it?
faq.answer: Yes. It converts code investigation into concise findings and plain-language replies.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
